Communication and Media

Erasmus University Rotterdam

← Back to search
About this programme

A reliable curriculum comparison is currently unavailable. The external curriculum has unresolved requirements; no complete degree pathway is certified here.

IBCoM at Erasmus studies communication and media from social, cultural, political and economic perspectives, with an international and comparative approach. Students study theory and research methods, develop communication skills, undertake an internship and complete an empirical thesis.

A complete UCR comparison is withheld because the regulations for students entering in 2026 do not yet establish a consistent 180-EC curriculum. This is a limit in the available curriculum evidence, not a conclusion that UCR offers no suitable study possibilities.

Academic year: 2026–2027

External pathway: 2026 entrants: minor pathway with International Communication & Business and Creative Industries & Audiences

The verified components below account for 175 EC of the 180-EC degree. The remaining 5 EC, including the credit status of the second-year research workshop, requires official clarification. This is an incomplete curriculum, not a certified degree plan.

Official programme source ↗
Verified partial curriculum — incomplete degree pathway

Only the verified components listed below are shown. They do not constitute a complete degree programme.

5 EC

International and Global Communication
5 EC

Quantitative Methods in Media and Communication
5 EC

Qualitative Methods in Media and Communication
5 EC

Communication Management
5 EC

Communication and Media Labour Market Orientation

Digital Content
5 EC

Communication Ethics
5 EC

Communication and Media Internship
12 EC
Compulsory 12-EC field-specific internship; all first-year courses must be completed before entry.


Bachelor Thesis
15 EC
Individual 15-EC empirical thesis. Entry requires first-year completion, at least 30 qualifying later-year EC, both methods courses and the second-year research workshop. Three interim assignments and a draft must be passed/submitted; the workshop credit allocation remains unresolved.


International Communication & Business focus-area courses
10 EC
Two 5-EC restricted-choice courses in International Communication & Business.


Creative Industries & Audiences focus-area courses
10 EC
Two 5-EC restricted-choice courses in Creative Industries & Audiences.


Open elective courses
20 EC
20 EC of genuine open elective study in one or more secondary fields.


Minor
15 EC
15-EC approved minor; students must be enrolled at least in their third year.
